shortName: TenKey LandCo I v. Simpson Cnty. Fiscal Court
citation: TenKey LandCo I, LLC v. Simpson Cnty. Fiscal Ct., No. 26-CI-00018 (Ky. Cir. Ct. Simpson Cnty. filed Jan. 2026).
corporateEntities: Tenkey Landco I, LLC; SPDJ Partners, LLC; OTN Development Company, LLC; “Project Lionsgate/Blackjack”
category: Land Use Planning and Zoning: Substantive Planning Decisions
summary: The developer TenKey LandCo filed this suit in January 2026 to strike down a county ordinance passed in December. The ordinance requires data centers to be located in heavy industrial zones and to obtain a conditional use permit. TenKey argues that under KRS Chapter 100, a city with its own independent planning commission has exclusive authority over land use inside its borders. Its attorney argued that a city "cannot be independent" if the county's authority overlaps its jurisdiction. TenKey stresses that its site lies entirely within Franklin and that the city has already found the project to be a permitted use. TenKey seeks a declaratory judgment that the ordinance cannot be enforced within Franklin's city limits or applied to TenKey. In May 2026 the court denied two procedural motions: One was TenKey's motion to disqualify the county's lawyers, and the other was the county's motion to stay the case. The case is ongoing.

shortName: Guido v. Columbia Cnty. Bd. of Comm'rs
citation: Guido v. Columbia Cty. Bd. of Comm'r, No. A26A2272 (Ga. Ct. App., filed June 16, 2026).
corporateEntities: White Oak Business Center; Pumpkin Center
category: Land Use Planning and Zoning: Substantive Planning Decisions
summary: A resident of Harlem, Georgia with pro se representation challenged the Columbia County Board of Commissioners rezoning decisions regarding multiple data centers and a quarry.   The cases were dismissed in March of 2026 and the plaintiff is seeking a consolidated appeal in the Georgia Court of Appeals. The appeal is ongoing as of October 2026.

shortName: Kentucky Industrial Alliance, LLC v. City of Cave City, the Cave City Council and the Joint City-County Planning Commission
citation: Kentucky Industrial Alliance, LLC v. City of Cave City, the Cave City Council and the Joint City-County Planning Commission
category: Land Use Planning and Zoning: Public Meeting and Notice Requirements
summary: In a second, related lawsuit, Kentucky Industrial Alliance (KIA) asked the Barren County Circuit Court to void Cave City's September 2024 annexation (Ordinance 24-9-9C) of the approximately 245-acre former Branstetter property where KIA's data center project is planned — arguing that if the annexation is invalid, the property would fall outside city jurisdiction and the city's data center moratorium (challenged in the companion case above) would not apply to it. KIA's complaint centers on a roughly 0.09-acre parcel containing the historic Shaw Cemetery within the annexed tract, alleging that Branstetter Family Holdings did not actually own the cemetery parcel (whose title traces to a 1902 deed) when it signed consent to the annexation, and that KIA — not Branstetter — was declared the cemetery's rightful successor-in-title by a December 2024 default judgment in unrelated litigation; KIA contends the entire annexation ordinance must be invalidated, rather than just the cemetery parcel excised from it, because the city intended to annex one unified site. This case has been consolidated with KIA's earlier moratorium challenge, with the annexation issue proceeding first since it could resolve the city's jurisdiction over the property entirely.

shortName: Paige v. Vantage Data Centers Management Company, LLC
citation: Paige v. Vantage Data Ctrs. Mgmt. Co., No. 1:24-cv-00777 (E.D. Va. dismissed June 11, 2025).
forum: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia
category: Corporate Tax, Securities, Employment and Lobbying: Employment
summary: Charles R. Paige filed suit against Vantage Data Centers Management Company LLC and Heather Rogers in the Virginia Eastern District Court on May 8, 2024, based on employment matters. The plaintiff alleges a violation of Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 under the pretext that defendant Vantage — his employer —  is responsible for sexual harassment and retaliation. Against defendant Rogers, who was plaintiff’s former supervisor, the allegation is related to battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress. Plaintiff sought compensatory damages, including economic and non-economic damages. On May 14, 2025, the parties settled a confidential extrajudicial agreement, and plaintiff filed the required registration and disclosed the campaign finances. In August 2025, the case was dismissed with prejudice.

shortName: Morgantown Power, LLC
citation: Morgantown Power, LLC, 196 FERC ¶ 61,075 (2026).
category: Energy Law: RTOs, FERC, DOE
summary: Morgantown Power, LLC (Morgantown Power) submitted an application to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) seeking authorizations necessary to engage in a transaction between Chesapeake Data, LLC (TeraWulf) and Lanyard Power Holdings, LLC (GenOn) pursuant to the Federal Power Act and Part 33 of the regulations of FERC. Morgantown Power owns and operates four oil-fired generating units with a combined generating capacity of about 216 MW located within the PJM Interconnection. In this transaction, GenOn will sell one hundred percent of the membership interests in Morgantown Power to TeraWulf. Morgantown Power claims that the proposed transaction. Morgantown Power requests a 21-day comment period and expedited consideration of the required authorizations for the transaction, pursuant to Sections 33.11(b) and (c) of FERC’s regulations. On July 29, 2026, FERC authorized the proposed transaction as consistent with the public interest.

shortName: Land Legacy, Inc. v. Ringle
citation: Land Legacy, Inc. v. Ringle, No. CJ-2026-00074 (Okla. Dist. Ct. Osage Cnty. filed Mar. 23, 2026).
category: Common Law: Property
summary: On March 23, 2026, Land Legacy, Inc. filed a lawsuit in the District Court of Osage County, Oklahoma, against Alan J. Ringle, Susan A. Ringle, Mark A. Ringle, Aaron J. Ringle, The Ringle Family, LLC, Ringle Development, L.L.C., and John Does 1–10. The plaintiff brought claims for declaratory judgment, breach of easement, trespass, and tortious interference, alleging that the defendants' pursuit of industrial development of a hyperscale data center violated the Deed of Conservation Easement and interfered with the plaintiff's contractual rights and business opportunities. The plaintiff sought a declaration that the easement prohibits proposed industrial development, a permanent injunction terminating and prohibiting violations of the easement, disgorgement of all monies by which the defendants had been unjustly enriched, compensatory and punitive damages each exceeding $75,000, prejudgment and postjudgment interest, and attorneys' fees and costs. On September 3, 2026, the court granted in part and denied in part the defendants' motion to dismiss, dismissing without prejudice the tortious interference claim and the plaintiff's standalone disgorgement theory based on tax deductions, while allowing the declaratory judgment, breach of easement, and trespass claims to proceed and granting leave to amend. On September 22, 2026, the plaintiff filed an amended petition adding Project Spring, LLC, White Rose Partners, LLC, Horizon Land Development, LLC, and Google, LLC as defendants and revising its tortious interference allegations. The case remains open, and no final decision appears in the available docket.

shortName: Citizens for Faquier Cnty. v. Town of Warrenton
citation:
Citizens for Fauquier Cnty. v. Town of Warrenton, 904 S.E.2d 213 (Va. Ct. App. 2024).
(Virginia court documents: 81 Va. App. 363, 904 S.E.2d 213 (2024).)
category: Information/Records Requests/Elections and Ballot Measures
summary: In 2022, Petitioner Citizens for Fauquier County (CFFC) submitted Virginia Freedom of Information Act requests to the Town of Warrenton. It asked for for emails and correspondence between town officials and Amazon about Amazon's proposed data center and its special use permit. The Town produced some records but withheld over 3100 emails under statutory exemptions. CFFC sought a writ of mandamus in the Fauquier County Circuit, which ruled for the Town in 2023, and CFFC appealed to the Court of Appeals of Virginia. In July 2024, the Court of Appeals held that the correspondence exemption applies to only one county official. It also remanded for further review of the withheld records and of attorney's fees. The appeal is closed. Separate litigation over the Amazon special use permit is still active in Fauquier County Circuit Court.

shortName: Tucker United v. Crowder
citation: Tucker United v. Crowder, No. 26-ICA-92 (W. Va. Intermediate Ct. App. filed Mar. 6, 2026), dismissed for lack of jurisdiction Aug. 26, 2026.
forum: Intermediate Court of Appeals of West Virginia
corporateEntities: Fundamental Data, Ridgeline Power Plant and Data Center
category: Environmental Law: Pollution Control
summary: Tucker United, the West Virginia Highlands Conservancy, and Sierra Club challenged the state Department of Environmental Protection’s issuance of an air permit to Fundamental Data, LLC for the proposed Ridgeline gas power station near Davis and Thomas, West Virginia. They alleged that WVDEP improperly classified the facility as a synthetic minor source, inadequately accounted for fugitive emissions and potential emissions, failed to require sufficient emissions testing and air-dispersion modeling, and improperly withheld permit information as confidential business information. The Air Quality Board denied all but one objection. The appellants appealed to the West Virginia Intermediate Court of Appeals, and their appeal was dismissed for lack of jurisdiction.

shortName: In re Appalachian Power Co.
citation: In re Appalachian Power Co. & Wheeling Power Co., No. 24-0611-E-T-PW (W. Va. Pub. Serv. Comm'n Mar. 25, 2025) (order).
summary: On July 18, 2024, Appalachian Power Company and Wheeling Power Company applied to the Public Service Commission of West Virginia to revise their Large Capacity Power and Industrial Power tariffs for prospective large electricity customers (i.e., Google). The proceeding concerns utility tariff regulation under W. Va. Code § 24-2-4a, including service commitments and protections against infrastructure and stranded-cost risks associated with large loads, including data centers. Google challenged the proposed contract duration and minimum electricity commitments, prompting negotiations in which the Commission's Consumer Advocate proposed a compromise modeled on Google's agreement with Indiana Michigan Power. The resulting settlement established a minimum 12-year contract term and an 80-percent minimum billing-demand requirement for qualifying new loads of at least 100 megawatts at an individual site or 150 megawatts in aggregate. On March 25, 2025, the Commission approved the tariff revisions, and the utilities filed revised tariff sheets in April 2025.

shortName: Switch, Ltd. v. NVLCO Storey Cnty., LLC
citation: Switch, Ltd. v. NVLCO Storey Cnty., LLC, No. 3:23-cv-00508 (D. Nev. filed Oct. 19, 2023).
forum: United States District Court for the District of Nevada
category: Common Law: Property
summary: On October 5, 2023, Switch, Ltd. and SUPERNAP Reno, LLC filed a lawsuit in Nevada’s First Judicial District Court in Storey County against NVLCO Storey County, LLC, SVO Nevada, LLC, and PSO Nevada, LLC. On October 19, 2023, NVLCO Storey County, LLC removed the action to the United States District Court for the District of Nevada. In their First Amended Complaint, filed on October 10, 2023, the plaintiffs brought claims for declaratory relief, breach of a restrictive covenant, breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, and tortious interference with prospective contracts, challenging the defendants’ intended use of a property for a data center. The plaintiffs sought declaratory relief concerning permissible use under the covenant, preliminary and permanent injunctions preventing data center development, monetary damages exceeding $15,000, pre-judgment and post-judgment interest, punitive damages, and costs, disbursements, and attorneys' fees. On November 15, 2023, the federal district court granted the plaintiffs' motion to remand the action to the First Judicial District Court in and for Storey County, granted the motion to seal, denied all other pending motions as moot, and closed the federal case. On August 21, 2024, the federal district court denied the plaintiffs' motion for attorneys' fees and costs.

shortName: Innovation 411 Fee Owner LLC v. Upper Merion Twp. Bd. of Supervisors
citation: Innovation 411 Fee Owner LLC v. Upper Merion Twp. Bd. of Supervisors, No. 2026-21467 (Pa. Ct. Com. Pl. Montgomery Cnty. filed Sep. 16, 2026).
forum: Montgomery County Court of Common Pleas
category: Land Use Planning and Zoning: Substantive Planning Decisions
summary: On September 16, 2026, Innovation 411 Fee Owner LLC, a developer affiliated with MLP Ventures, filed a land-use appeal in the Court of Common Pleas of Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, against the Upper Merion Township Board of Supervisors. The appeal was one of five challenging the Board's August 13, 2026 denials of preliminary land development plans for a proposed data center campus in King of Prussia. In the September appeals, the developer argued that the proposed data center use was permitted under the Township's zoning code because Township officials had previously treated data centers as warehouses. The developer sought relief across those appeals, including reversal of the Board's decisions, preliminary approval of the plans, and appointment of an independent referee to conduct an evidentiary hearing. The case remains open, and no final decision appears in the available docket.

shortName: Request for Rehearing, Motion to Intervene, and Motion for Stay, Re U.S. Dep't of Energy Order Nos. 202-25-12 & 202-25-13
citation: Request for Rehearing, Motion to Intervene, and Motion for Stay, Re U.S. Dep't of Energy Order Nos. 202-25-12 & 202-25-13 (Jan. 22, 2026).
docket: U.S. Dep't of Energy Order Nos. 202-25-12 & 202-25-13
category: Energy Law: RTOs, FERC, DOE
summary: Starting in May 2025, DOE issued emergency directives under Sec. 202(c) of the Federal Power Act to prevent retirement of coal plants across the country. Several of these orders have been challenged in court and on FERC dokets by states, environmental and public interest organizations on the grounds that rather than being responsive to emergencies they are instead usurping resource adequacy planning and abridging state jurisdiction over retirements. Over 60 orders have been issued to date, including the plant at issue here, Culley 2 in Indiana.

shortName: In PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 189 FERC ¶ 61,078 (2024), order on reh'g, 191 FERC ¶ 61,025 (2025)
citation: PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 189 FERC ¶ 61,078 (2024), order on reh'g, 191 FERC ¶ 61,025 (2025).
category: Energy Law: RTOs, FERC, DOE
summary: On November 1, 2024, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC”), pursuant to section 205 of the Federal Power Act, issued an order rejecting an amended Interconnection Service Agreement (ISA) among PJM Interconnection, LLC (PJM), Susquehanna Nuclear, LLC (Susquehanna), and PPL Electric Utilities Corporation (PPL). The proposed amended ISA would increase the amount of co-located load at the Susquehanna facility from 300 megawatts (MW) to 480 MW. Susquehanna subsequently filed a request for rehearing of the Rejection Order, and Vistra Corp. filed a motion for clarification of the Rejection Order. PJM’s proposed amended ISA included provisions non-conforming with the transmission provider’s pro-forma interconnection agreement, which FERC has recognized may be permissible for interconnections that can show specific reliability concerns, novel legal issues, or other unique factors. In rejecting the amended ISA, FERC found that PJM did not meet its burden to demonstrate specific reliability concerns, novel legal issues, or other unique factors that would permit PJM to deviate from the pro forma ISA. In petitioning for a rehearing, Susquehanna contended that the Rejection Order failed to apply the correct legal standard, to address record evidence that shows the Amended ISA satisfies this standard, and to reasonably explain its ultimate conclusion. FERC sustained the result of the Rejection Order for the same reasons as previously. Vistra asked FERC to clarify that the Rejection Order did not intend to impose a blanket limit on interconnection service to generators co-located with data centers or prevent the use of non-conforming interconnection agreements to obtain such service. FERC declined to make Vistra’s clarification exactly as requested and instead clarified that the Commission used the necessary standard to determine whether the filing of a non-conforming agreement is justified. FERC also clarified that the Rejection Order does not prejudge any future filing or prevent entities from filing non-conforming interconnection agreements. Susquehanna subsequently appealed in Federal Court.

shortName: Greenidge Generation LLC v. New York State Dep't of Environmental Conservation
citation: Greenidge Generation LLC v. N.Y. State Dep’t of Env’t Conservation, 86 Misc. 3d 338 (Sup. Ct. 2024).
category: Environmental Law: Adequacy of Environmental Review
summary: Green Ridge Generation LLC sued the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation in the New York Supreme Court, Yates County, challenging the Department’s denial of its application to renew a Clean Air Act Title V permit for its power plant. Green Ridge sued under New York State administrative law and the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act. The Supreme Court rejected Green Ridge's challenge, and Green Ridge appealed. The New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Fourth Department, summarily dismissed the appeal. See Greenidge Generation, LLC v. New York State Dep't of Env't Conservation, 246 A.D.3d 1374 (N.Y.A.D. 4 Dept. 2026).

shortName: Georgia Interfaith Power & Light v. Georgia Public Service Comm'n
citation: Ga. Interfaith Power & Light v. Ga. Pub. Serv. Comm’n, No. 26CV004316 (Ga. Super. Ct. Fulton Cnty. filed Mar. 25, 2026) (petition for judicial review of Ga. Pub. Serv. Comm’n Docket Nos. 56298 & 56310).
summary: On March 25, 2026, Georgia Interfaith Power & Light, Park Avenue Baptist Church, Unitarian Universalist Church of Savannah, Sierra Club, Adrien Webber, and Southern Alliance for Clean Energy petitioned a Georgia superior court for judicial review of Georgia Public Service Commission orders approving Georgia Power's proposed generation resources. The petition invokes Georgia administrative judicial-review law, O.C.G.A. § 50-13-19, and electric-generation certification requirements under O.C.G.A. § 46-3A-4. Petitioners contend the Commission approved resources without required findings of need and sufficient evidentiary support, exposing ratepayers to unnecessary costs. They seek reversal and remand of the certification orders, including decertification of at least 757 megawatts. The Commission issued its initial certification order on December 30, 2025, and affirmed it on February 23, 2026; no final court disposition was verified as of October 20, 2026.

shortName: In re Interstate Power & Light Co.
citation: In re Interstate Power & Light Co., Docket No. GCU-2026-0005 (Iowa Utils. Comm'n filed Sep. 11, 2026).
summary: Interstate Power and Light (Alliant Energy) sought a certificate of public convenience from the Iowa Utilities Commission for a 1200 MW gas plant. The Office of Consumer Advocate is seeking a public hearing and proof the project is cost effective while the utiliity is claiming it is more appropriate to address those issues in a future rate case.

citation: E. Kahn Dev. Corp. v. Township of Montgomery, No. SOM-L-001072-26 (N.J. Super. Ct. Law Div. Somerset Cnty. July 31, 2026).
forum: Superior Court of New Jersey Law Division: Somerset County
category: Land Use Planning and Zoning: Substantive Planning Decisions

shortName: Cresa Global Inc. v. Chirisa Capital Management (US) LLC
citation: Cresa Glob. Inc. v. Chirisa Cap. Mgmt. (US) LLC, C.A. No. N24C-07-223-SKR CCLD (Del. Super. Ct. Jan. 9, 2025).
category: Common Law: Contract Disputes Among Developers
summary: Plaintiff Cresa Global Inc. brought suit against Defendant Chirisa Capital Management, a VA data center owner and operator. Plaintiffs say that they procured a client, CoreWeave, Inc., to lease the site from the Defendants via a Master Services Agreement for data center Services at the site. Plaintiffs were not included as a party to the MSA, but say they are owed a transaction commission for their labor. Defendants do not agree. No written agreement was ever formally written between the parties. The court held that the Defendants’ motion to dismiss the claims was denied. The Defendants claimed that DE was a less convenient forum than VA to litigate but could not sufficiently demonstrate why this was the case.

shortName: Milwaukee Riverkeeper, Inc. v. City of Racine
citation: Milwaukee Riverkeeper, Inc. v. City of Racine, No. 2025CV001240 (Wis. Cir. Ct. Racine Cnty. Oct. 7, 2025).
category: Information/Records Requests/Elections and Ballot Measures
summary: Racine’s water utility provides water to Microsoft’s $3.3 billion data center project in Mount Pleasant under an agreement between Racine and Mount Pleasant. In February 2025, Milwaukee Riverkeeper submitted a public records request on Microsoft’s projected water use, and the group says the city gave no response for more than 100 days. Eventually, the water utility director said the data could not be released because it was classified as trade secrets under the Wisconsin Uniform Trade Secrets Act and therefore could be withheld under the state’s public records law. On September 15, 2025, Midwest Environmental Advocates filed suit on behalf of Milwaukee Riverkeeper against the City of Racine, the Racine Water Utility, and the executive director of the Racine Water Utility in Racine County Circuit Court as a petition for writ of mandamus. On September 17, 2025, the city released data showing that Microsoft’s data centers will require up to 8.4 million gallons of water a year. On October 7, 2025, Milwaukee Riverkeeper filed a notice of voluntary dismissal under Wis. Stat. § 805.04(1), and the case was dismissed.

shortName: Aligned Data Centers Phoenix LLC v. DPR Construction
citation: Aligned Data Centers Phoenix Propco LLC v. DPR Construction, No. CV2019-015648 (Ariz. Super. Ct. Maricopa Cnty. filed Dec. 23, 2019).
forum: Superior Court of Arizona in Maricopa County
category: Common Law: Contract Disputes Among Developers
summary: On December 24, 2019, Aligned Data Centers Propco, LLC (“Plaintiff”), a data center company, sued DPR Construction (“DPR”), which indemnified Rosendin Electric, Inc. (“REI”) in the Superior Court of Arizona in Maricopa County. Under Plaintiff’s contract with defendant DPR, DPR was responsible for soliciting subcontractors to perform necessary work. DPR hired REI to perform the electrical work on the data center. Plaintiff claimed that defendant DPR breached the contract when REI personnel, under the oversight and direction of DPR, violated written procedures, guidelines, and warnings and failed to install a lock on a switch. Plaintiff further claimed that this failure resulted in personnel manually turning a switch the wrong direction, which caused an outage of all electrical service in the data center. Plaintiff claimed that this outage caused Plaintiff and its customers substantial harm, for which Plaintiff sought damages from DPR. DPR then sought indemnification from REI.  On August 8, 2022 this matter was dismissed with prejudice as to all parties.

shortName: People v. DOE
citation: Michigan v. U.S. Dep’t of Energy, No. 25-1159, slip op. (D.C. Cir. Sept. 11, 2026).
forum: United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit
category: Energy Law: RTOs, FERC, DOE
summary: On July 24, 2025, the State of Michigan petitioned the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit for review of the Department of Energy’s ("DOE") Interpretation of section 202(c) of the Federal Power Act. The State of Michigan claimed that the Department of Energy illegally used a short-term, federal emergency authority conferred in section 202(c) of the Federal Power Act to order the aging coal-fired J.H. Campbell Generating Plant to stay open after it was scheduled to shut down in 2025. On September 11, 2026, the Court vacated the DOE’s order and held that the DOE’s interpretation of the nature and scope of its emergency authority under section 202(c) exceeded its statutory authority.

shortName: Virginia Electric and Power Company - For approval of a Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity to construct/operate the proposed Chesterfield Energy and approval of designated Rider CERC
citation: Nat’l Ass’n for Advancement of Colored People-Chesterfield Branch v. State Corp. Comm’n, No. 260476 (Va. filed May 27, 2026).
summary: The NAACP Chesterfield Branch appeals to the Supreme Court of Virginia from the State Corporation Commission proceeding, Case No. PUR-2025-00037. There, the State Corporation Commission approved Dominion Energy’s Chesterfield Energy Reliability Center, a gas power plant. The appeal alleges violations of the Virginia State Air Pollution Control Law, the Virginia Administrative Process Act, the Virginia Environmental Justice Act, and the federal Clean Air Act. The case is pending as of October 2026.

shortName: Hatfield v. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
citation: Hatfield v. U.S. Army Corps of Eng'rs, No. 3:25-cv-00714 (S.D.W. Va. filed Dec. 3, 2025).
forum: United States District Court for the Southern District of West Virginia
category: Environmental Law: Adequacy of Environmental Review
summary: Danny Hatfield filed suit alongside eight other individuals against TransGas Development Systems, LLC and three federal agencies: the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. The lawsuit invokes several federal environmental and regulatory laws, specifically the Endangered Species Act, the Clean Water Act, the National Environmental Policy Act, and the Natural Gas Act. The plaintiffs sought to prevent TransGas from proceeding with the construction of the Adams Fork Energy Project, which includes a power plant, ammonia facility, and data centers, until the involved federal agencies satisfy their required statutory reviews, consultations, and permitting processes. The Court dismissed claims against TransGas without prejudice in March 2026. The remaining claims against the federal agencies are pending as of October 2026.

citation: In re MZX Tech, LLC, PSD Permit No. 0680-00119 (Miss. Env’t Quality Permit Bd. petition for hearing filed Apr. 9, 2026)
corporateEntities: XAI; MZX Tech., LLC; Anthropic; MacrohardRR
category: Environmental Law: Pollution Control
summary: Southern Environmental Law Center petitioned the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality for a formal hearing challenging its issuance of a construction permit that would allow MZX Tech, LLC to install 41 power-generating turbines. Southern Environmental Law Center alleges that the Department violated Mississippi environmental laws requiring emission offsets to mitigate the environmental impact. Southern Environmental Law Center also alleges that the Department failed to follow procedural laws that require agencies to hold meetings open to the public.

shortName: In re Ohio Power Co.
citation: In re Application of Ohio Power Co. for New Tariffs Related to Data Centers & Mobile Data Centers, No. 24-508-EL-ATA (Pub. Utils. Comm'n of Ohio July 9, 2025).
summary: On May 13, 2024, Ohio Power Company filed an application with the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio seeking approval of new tariffs for data centers and mobile data centers. The proceeding concerns Ohio public utility ratemaking and tariff regulation under Ohio Revised Code § 4909.18, particularly the allocation of infrastructure costs associated with large electricity loads. Data center operators, technology companies, manufacturers, retailers, energy suppliers, and consumer advocacy organizations, including the Office of the Ohio Consumers’ Counsel, participated in the proceeding. On July 9, 2025, the Commission approved a settlement establishing a data center tariff designed to address large-load costs and protect other customers. The Commission denied applications for rehearing on September 3, 2025, and its decision was subsequently appealed to the Supreme Court of Ohio in Case No. 2025-1458.

shortName: Amazon Data Services, Inc. v. PacifiCorp
citation: Amazon Data Servs., Inc. v. PacifiCorp, No. UM 2410 (Or. Pub. Util. Comm'n filed Oct. 30, 2025) (complaint).
summary: On October 30, 2025, Amazon Data Services, Inc. filed a complaint against PacifiCorp, doing business as Pacific Power, before the Public Utility Commission of Oregon concerning electricity service to four proposed data center campuses. The complaint raises issues involving utility service obligations, exclusive service territories, and contractual duties under electric service agreements, including ORS §§ 757.020 and 757.603. Amazon alleges that PacifiCorp provided insufficient electricity to one campus, failed to provide service to another, and refused to complete service arrangements for two additional campuses, while also disputing certain utility charges. Amazon seeks orders requiring PacifiCorp to fulfill its service obligations or, alternatively, removing the affected campuses from its exclusive service territory. PacifiCorp filed an answer, counterclaims, and a partial motion to dismiss in December 2025; an administrative law judge denied the dismissal motion on February 19, 2026. The parties obtained multiple procedural extensions, including a September 22, 2026 ruling. An October 14, 2026 protective-order filing reflected continued administrative activity without a final Commission decision.

documents.title: Complaint
documents.description: Amazon Data Services alleges PacifiCorp failed to deliver contracted power to four Oregon data center campuses and improperly demanded a 32.6 percent tax gross-up, and asks the Commission to compel service or remove the sites from PacifiCorp's exclusive service territory.

shortName: Overhue v. Brown
citation: Overhue v. Brown, No. 26WE-CC00131 (30th Jud. Cir.. Webster Cty, Mo., filed Oct. 5, 2026)
forum: "Circuit Court of Webster County, Missouri (30th Judicial Circuit)"
category: Common Law: Torts
summary: The developer of a controversial data center filed a defamation lawsuit against a candidate for Webster County Presiding Commissioner. It focuses on false claims made by the defendent about development of electrical and cooling systems and a video about the noise from a generator which the plaintiff claims were just from testing and not a long-term noise impact on residents. He is claiming that this has caused him reputational and financial damage.

shortName: We Are Mason Cnty., KY, Inc. v. Mason Cnty.
citation: We Are Mason Cnty., KY, Inc. v. Mason Cnty. Fiscal Ct., No. 26-CI-00091 (Ky. Cir. Ct. Mason Cnty. June 23, 2026) (order of dismissal).
category: Land Use Planning and Zoning: Substantive Planning Decisions
summary: The nonprofit We Are Mason County and other residents filed a "Complaint, Appeal, and Petition for Declaration of Rights" on March 26, 2026, challenging a multi-phase hyperscale data center project for an anonymous developer (discovered in October 2026 to be Meta). The group argued that rezoning thousands of acres for a massive data center complex violated the county's existing zoning plan. The suit challenged Ordinance 26-01, adopted February 27, 2026, as an appeal under KRS 100.347. That ordinance created land use classifications for data centers and amended the land use charts. On June 23, 2026, the presiding judge dismissed every count. He held that the plaintiffs had no statutory standing because the ordinance was not a map amendment and did not affect their land. He found the declaratory judgment counts presented no actual controversy. He also found that limits on speaking time and written comments did not deny due process. The same group and other residents then filed a second complaint against the fiscal court, the planning commission, the industrial authority, and many landowners. The seven counts in the complaint include a KRS 100.213 violation, lack of substantial evidence, spot zoning from A-2 to I-3, an application not filed by the real party in interest, an incomplete application, a declaration of rights, and nuisance. It asks the court to reverse the rezoning and to issue an injunction, or in the alternative, to award damages for lost property value. In October 2026, the fiscal court approved a development agreement. More than 2,000 acres have been zoned for it.

shortName: State ex rel. Bristolville 25 Developer LLC v. Village of Lordstown
citation: State ex rel. Bristolville 25 Developer LLC v. Vill. of Lordstown, No. 2025-1497 (Ohio filed Nov. 12, 2025)
category: Land Use Planning and Zoning: Substantive Planning Decisions
summary: The State of Ohio ex rel. Bristolville 25 Developer LLC and BHGH Properties LLC sued the Village of Lordstown, Kellie Bordner (zoning administrator), and Matthew Ries (village solicitor) in the Ohio Supreme Court, claiming that on Oct. 20, 2025 the Village declined to process Bristolville’s application that would initiate the zoning permit process for a proposed data center project. They are seeking a writ of mandamus to have the Village accept, review, and act upon Bristolville’s submission under Lordstown Codified Ordinance 1115 and using the Site Plan Review Process in effect as of Oct. 20, 2025. The case against Matthew Ries was dismissed on Dec. 24, 2025, but the lawsuit against the other parties remains ongoing as of October 2026.

shortName: City of Imperial v. Cnty. of Imperial
citation: City of Imperial v. Cnty. of Imperial, No. ECU004457 (Cal. Super. Ct. Imperial Cnty. Sept. 9, 2026) (decision on petitions for writ of mandate).
category: Land Use Planning and Zoning: Substantive Planning Decisions
summary: City of Imperial filed a petition for a writ of mandate and declaratory relief against the County of Imperial and its Board of Supervisors. The case was filed in Imperial County Superior Court. In this case, the City challenges the county's treatment of the Imperial Valley Data Center, a data center campus at Aten and Clark Rds., as a ministerial, by-right project exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), along with related grading permits and the lot merger. The court initially found the City's pleading legally insufficient and allowed it to amend, and denied an emergency halt in Apr. 2026. The Sierra Club later joined as a petitioner. After a trial on July 29, 2026, the court issued a tentative decision on Aug. 31 and a ruling on Sep. 9, 2026. It held that the County prejudicially abused its discretion by approving the lot merger without CEQA review, that a full environmental impact report is required, and that the challenged approvals and exemption notices must be set aside; it declined to invalidate the 2017 ordinance allowing data centers in industrial zones. The developer has said it will seek a new trial and, if denied, appeal. The case is still open as of October 2026.

shortName: State of California v. Wright
citation: State of California v. Wright
forum: United States District Court for the Northern District of California
category: Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers
summary: California and twelve other states (along with California's Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development) sued U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright, the Department of Energy, and the Office of Management and Budget, alleging the administration unlawfully terminated federal funding for energy and infrastructure programs established under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and Inflation Reduction Act — including roughly $1.2 billion in funding for California's ARCHES clean-hydrogen hub and funding for Washington's Pacific Northwest Hydrogen Hub. Plaintiffs allege the terminations, based on a May 2025 DOE policy memorandum, exceeded executive authority, violated the constitutional separation of powers by overriding congressionally appropriated funds, and were arbitrary and capricious in violation of the Administrative Procedure Act; they seek declaratory and injunctive relief restoring the funding.

shortName: FX Solutions v. Broad Reach Power, LLC
citation: FX Solutions LLC v. EnCap Investments L.P., No. DV-56-2026-0000081-OC (Mont. Dist. Ct. Yellowstone County filed Jan. 9, 2026).
corporateEntities: FX Solutions; Encap; Quantica; Broad Reach Power; Engie
category: Common Law: Contract Disputes Among Developers
summary: Plaintiff FX Solutions (an MT company) brought a claim against defendant Quantica Infrastructure (a TX developer). EnCap Investments is Quantica’s financial backer (and self-describes as a “leading provider of growth capital to independent energy companies”). Plaintiff claims that Quantica’s subsidiary, Broad Reach Power, offered to provide 300 megawatts of electricity on the condition that FX Solutions sell a tract of land. Plaintiff claims detrimental reliance on a broken promise made by Quantica to sell the tract of land for $5.5 million. Plaintiff asserts that he never received the promised electricity, and that Quantica is now using the land FX Solutions sold as a location for a new data center spanning 5k acres in Broadview, MT. Plaintiff claims that this data center deal was effectively stolen from him through his detrimental reliance on Quantica, causing a financial loss of billions that could have been earned from the data center construction. The plaintiff seeks damages for breach of contract, breach of good-faith dealing, and unjust enrichment. The case is pending as of November, 2026.

shortName: Great Lakes Neighbors, Inc. v. City of Port Washington Joint Review Bd.
citation: Great Lakes Neighbors, Inc. v. City of Port Washington Joint Rev. Bd., No. 2026CV000001 (Wis. Cir. Ct. dismissed Sep. 16, 2026).
corporateEntities: Vantage Data Center "Lighthouse"; Open AI; Oracle
category: Land Use Planning and Zoning: Substantive Planning Decisions
summary: A local grassroots nonprofit called Great Lakes Neighbors, Inc. filed a lawsuit against the City of Port Washington Joint Review Board after the board authorized approximately $175 million in municipal infrastructure improvements to support a data center campus being developed by Vantage Data Centers for OpenAI and Oracle. Plaintiffs challenged the creation of the city's Tax Incremental District No. 5 to help finance such improvements, alleging that the city failed to comply with legal requirements in establishing the District. The case was dismissed with prejudice on procedural grounds in September 2026.

shortName: PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 193 FERC ¶ 61,070 (2025).
citation: PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 193 FERC ¶ 61,217 (2025).
category: Energy Law: RTOs, FERC, DOE
summary: December 18, 2025, FERC issued a final order determining that PJM’s Open Access Transmission Tariff is “unjust and unreasonable” pursuant to section 206 of the Federal Power Act because its rules lacked clarity for interconnection customers serving loads such as AI data centers that are co-located with energy generation. FERC ordered PJM to propose revised tariff language, including three new alternative transmission service options. FERC also established a paper hearing to determine just and reasonable rates and conditions for new services. FERC also took issue with PJM’s Behind-the-Meter Generation rules (“BTMG”) and declared them “no longer just and reasonable,” and directed PJM to also revise its BTMG rules and submit a report on the reliability impacts of data centers and other large-load customers.

shortName: Steven O'Brien v. Cohere A9, LLC
citation: O'Brien v. Cohere A9, LLC, No. 655148/2016 (N.Y. Sup. Ct. Jan. 31, 2018).
category: Corporate Tax, Securities and Lobbying: Securities
summary: Steven O'Brien, as members' representative, filed a petition against Cohere A9, LLC in the Supreme Court of the State of New York. Under CPLR 7510 and 7514, the petitioner filed a petition seeking to confirm an arbitration award issued in the petitioner's favor. In that case, the petitioner was awarded the amount of $400,000 due to an amount withheld by the respondent when it acquired Another 9. On October 31, 2018, the court granted the petition and confirmed the award.
